text:
maria: thinking out loud — we need a 'budget-thermostat' guard for rollouts. idea: evaluate token-spend rate per-tenant over a rolling window and either divert traffic to cheaper model variants or pause the rollout when spend crosses a threshold. wants low-latency SLO checks combined with cost signals.

raj: +1. important: define evaluation window and min samples. we shouldn't flip on a single spike. maybe 5m window, min 200 requests?

samir: prefer diversion to an explicit pause by default. e.g. 20% -> 0% can be jarring. diversion options: split-reduce, route to smaller-quantized variant, or reduce max_tokens. also need an escape hatch for errors (5xx).

clair: for console UX: slider for $/min threshold, quick presets (dev, staging, prod), a "preview" that simulates what would have happened over last 24h, and an indicator showing how many tenants currently at risk. also show hysteresis controls (how long to wait before resume).

kevin: telemetry note: we need to compute per-route and per-tenant p95 latency, 5xx rate, token_spend_rate (tokens/sec or $/min). guards should be boolean expressions over those metrics with a min-sample requirement. also store the last N evaluations for audit.

maria: agree on audit trail. also the guard should include an ordered list of actions: 1) reduce split by X%, 2) route remainder to fallback model, 3) if still breaching, pause. order should be configurable per-rollout.

raj: pseudocode DSL sketch:

```yaml
guard: 
  name: budget-thermostat
  window: 5m
  min_requests: 250
  conditions:
    - metric: token_spend_per_minute
      op: ">"
      value: 0.08   # $0.08 / min threshold (example)
    - metric: p95_latency_ms
      op: ">"
      value: 600
  action_sequence:
    - type: reduce_split
      amount_percent: 30
    - type: route_to_fallback
      target: model-small-quant
    - type: pause_rollout
  resume_policy:
    cleared_for: 10m
    require_no_violation: 2  # two consecutive windows
```

samir: add note: fallback target must be capacity-aware. if fallback is slower, we might violate latency SLO even more. fallback selection should consider both cost and confirmed throughput on that model.

kevin: +1. suggest composite guard semantics: (cost AND (errors OR latency)) to avoid pausing for pure cost spikes that aren't affecting reliability. or allow customers to set cost-only mode.

maria: UX question — for A/B experiments, what does partial diversion look like? e.g., can we automatically rebalance traffic from variant B -> A by X% when guard fires, but still keep experiment metrics tracked? we need to keep attribution intact.

clair: yes — in the console show "safety split" overlay: baseline split vs live split, with notes about attribution and how experiment metrics will be normalized. show a warning banner: "safety rules altered split; experiment needs rebalancing to compare."

raj: implementation gotcha: guard evaluation must be idempotent and cheap. we should pre-aggregate token spend and error counts at the edge collector and only evaluate guards on central service with small payloads. avoid heavy queries during high load.

maria: what about tenant budgets at different tiers? e.g., free tier thresholds should be lower and enforcement stronger (auto-pause vs divert). should be configurable by tenant-plan mapped to guard presets.

samir: also think about grace-mode: when guard fires, throttle new sessions but let in-flight requests finish; don't cut KV caches mid-stream.

kevin: incident log example from canary earlier today (deploy-bot):

"deploy-bot: [1997770203] canary rollout for model-x started: 10% -> 50% over 20m. [1997770308] budget-thermostat guard triggered for tenant=acme-corp: token_spend_per_minute=0.12 > threshold 0.08. action: reduce_split 40% -> routed remainder to model-x-small. resume timer set 10m."

maria: nice. we should surface that exact log line in the rollout timeline in Console and make it clickable to expand the evaluation window and metrics.

clair: UI mock tasks: show 3 things in the rollout detail pane — 1) guard config (with edit option), 2) live signal graph with thresholds, 3) action history with ability to "force override" (admins only). I'll mock by EOD.

raj: next steps: I'll prototype the guard evaluator service (lightweight), samir will create a fallback selection policy, clair will do the mock, kevin will add telemetry pre-aggregates. maria will own requirements and coordinate product sign-off.

maria: thanks team. small follow-ups: define default thresholds for "prod" preset, and decide default action order (divert -> reduce -> pause). posting a doc with numbers in #eng-platform-docs once we agree. :thumbsup:

kevin: one more — add an emergency global kill switch key for SRE to immediately cut all rollouts in region if we see systemic cost/latency blowups. log as high-priority.

maria: yep — add to both the API and the Console (big red button).

deploy-bot: [1997770448] note: guard-eval-service v0.3 deployed to canary infra.

maria: great, closing this thread — will ping when doc is up.
